title: Derivative of the Gaussian distribution function
statement: Let $\Phi(t)=\gamma((-�\infty,t])$ be the distribution function of the standard Gaussian measure, whose density is $\varphi(t)=e^{-t^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$. For every $t\in\mathbb R$, $\Phi$ is differentiable at $t$ and $\Phi'(t)=\varphi(t)$.
replaced: Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$ and $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\varphi(x)\,dx$. For every $t\in\mathbb R$, the function $\Phi$ is differentiable at $t$ with derivative $\Phi'(t)=\varphi(t)$.
